subject.title: fix(gateway): restrict backend self-pairing shared auth

question: Should Gateway/security owners accept removing shared token/password from local backend self-pairing scope preservation now, after rebasing this PR onto the current local shared-auth behavior?
rationale: The code change is narrow and security-positive, but it intentionally changes a documented shipped auth boundary and may fail closed for existing local backend callers.

options.title: Rebase and accept hardened boundary
options.body: Resolve the current conflicts, preserve current-main local shared-auth behavior, and merge after explicit Gateway/security acceptance of the compatibility break.

options.title: Add a transition path first
options.body: If shipped backend callers rely on shared-token/password scope preservation, require a tested warning, migration, or compatibility window before fail-closed behavior lands.

options.title: Pause for broader auth design
options.body: If maintainers want to revisit the whole trusted-loopback operator model, pause this PR in favor of a broader Gateway auth design item.

recommendation.title: Rebase and accept hardened boundary
recommendation.body: Resolve the current conflicts, preserve current-main local shared-auth behavior, and merge after explicit Gateway/security acceptance of the compatibility break.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS assigns the touched Gateway auth and security-doc surfaces to this team.
